title: Impact of Medicaid Expansion on Uninsured Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
For this research scenario, a Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach is suitable because we have a clear division between treated and control groups (states that did and did not expand Medicaid coverage, respectively) and distinct pre- and post-treatment periods. The key identification assumption is that, in the absence of treatment, the trend in the uninsured rate would have been the same between treated and untreated states. This is known as the parallel trends assumption.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s31_data.csv"
data <- read_csv(data_path)

# Run the Difference-in-Differences regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated * post, data = data)

# Extract and print the coefficient of the interaction term (treat_x_post)
summary_did <- summary(did_model)
interaction_coeff <- summary_did$coefficients["treated:post", "Estimate"]
interaction_se <- summary_did$coefficients["treated:post", "Std. Error"]

# Robust standard errors
robust_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(did_model, type="HC1")["treated:post", "treated:post"])

# Print the result
cat("Coefficient for Treatment x Post:", interaction_coeff, "\n")
cat("Standard Error (Robust):", robust_se, "\n")

# Basic robustness check: removing states with extreme changes (outliers)
# Calculate residuals and find outliers
residuals <- resid(did_model)
outlier_threshold <- 2 * sd(residuals)
data_no_outliers <- data[abs(residuals) < outlier_threshold, ]

# Re-run the regression without outliers
did_model_no_outliers <- lm(y ~ treated * post, data = data_no_outliers)
summary_did_no_outliers <- summary(did_model_no_outliers)

# Extract and print the coefficient from the outlier-adjusted regression
interaction_coeff_no_outliers <- summary_did_no_outliers$coefficients["treated:post", "Estimate"]
robust_se_no_outliers <- sqrt(vcovHC(did_model_no_outliers, type="HC1")["treated:post", "treated:post"])

cat("Coefficient for Treatment x Post (no outliers):", interaction_coeff_no_outliers, "\n")
cat("Standard Error (Robust, no outliers):", robust_se_no_outliers, "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I anticipate finding a negative coefficient for the `treat_x_post` interaction term, indicating that Medicaid expansion in treated states is associated with a reduction in the uninsured rate compared to states that did not adopt the policy. The magnitude of the coefficient will likely reflect a moderate decrease, depending on the extent of the expansion and the baseline uninsured rates in treated states. The presence of robustness checks, such as removal of outliers, ensures that the results are not driven by extreme values, thus supporting the validity of the findings.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in uninsured rates over time between treated and untreated states.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of Medicaid coverage significantly reduces the uninsured rate.
